title: Customer Experience Report: NPS, CSAT and Effort Scores by Channel, Verbatim Sentiment Themes, Journey Pain Points, and Improvement Action Plan
subtitle: Customer Experience Report — Channel NPS, CSAT & Effort; Sentiment Themes, Journey Pain Points & Improvement Plan

document_brief.narrative_theme: Q1 2026 customer experience performance shows digital self-service lifting NPS while contact-center effort and specific journey pain points are driving detractors, guiding a focused 90-day improvement plan by channel and journey stage.

sections.heading: Q1 2026 CX Scorecard by Channel (NPS, CSAT, and Customer Effort)
key_facts: In Q1 2026, overall NPS was +18, with Mobile App at +42 and Phone Support at -6.
In Q1 2026, CSAT was 84% overall, with Live Chat at 90% and Email Support at 78%.
In Q1 2026, Customer Effort Score (1=low effort, 7=high effort) was 3.2 overall, with Phone Support at 4.6 and Mobile App at 2.1.

sections.heading: Verbatim Sentiment Themes, Journey Pain Points, and 90-Day Customer Improvement Action Plan
key_facts: From 12,480 verbatims collected between 2026-01-01 and 2026-03-31, the top negative theme was 'Wait time & transfers' at 31% of detractor comments.
The highest-friction journey stage in Q1 2026 was 'Billing & Payments' with an average Effort Score of 4.4, versus 2.5 for 'Onboarding'.
The 90-day action plan targets a +10 point increase in Phone Support NPS (from -6 to +4) by 2026-06-30.

spec.title: Q1 2026 Customer Experience Performance Summary
spec.subtitle: Ref: CX-1401925-Q1 | Date: 07 April 2026 | From: Customer Insights & Journey Analytics

sections.heading: Executive Overview
sections.body: For Q1 2026, overall Net Promoter Score (NPS) improved to +34, up 6 points quarter-over-quarter, primarily driven by higher satisfaction with digital self-service channels. Customer Satisfaction (CSAT) averaged 86%, while Customer Effort Score (CES, 1–5 scale) rose slightly to 3.4, indicating increased friction in assisted channels. Detractors are concentrated in contact-center interactions and late-stage service journeys. The results indicate strong digital momentum but persistent friction in human-assisted touchpoints.

sections.heading: Channel Performance Breakdown
sections.body: Digital self-service (web and mobile app) achieved an NPS of +48 and CSAT of 91%, supported by faster login authentication and simplified account dashboards. In contrast, voice support NPS declined to +12, with CSAT at 78% and CES at 3.9, reflecting long hold times and repeat transfers. Live chat stabilized at +29 NPS with 84% CSAT, though sentiment flagged inconsistency in agent knowledge. Email support remained flat at +18 NPS with extended response times averaging 42 hours.

sections.heading: Verbatim Sentiment Themes
sections.body: Promoters frequently cited ease of bill payment, intuitive navigation, and proactive outage notifications within the mobile app. Passives mentioned satisfactory issue resolution but inconsistent response speed when escalations were required. Detractors highlighted repeated authentication steps during phone calls, difficulty reaching a live agent, and confusion around service upgrade eligibility. Sentiment tagging shows a 22% increase in mentions of "long wait" and a 17% rise in comments referencing "being transferred multiple times."

sections.heading: Journey Pain Points
sections.body: The onboarding journey shows friction during identity verification, where 14% of applicants abandon after document upload errors. In the billing dispute journey, 28% of customers contact support after failing to locate clarification in FAQs, signaling a content gap. Service outage resolution remains a key pain point, with customers reporting limited status transparency during restoration windows. These journey-stage breakdowns correlate strongly with detractor segments in post-interaction surveys.

sections.heading: 90-Day Improvement Action Plan
sections.body: The CX team will pilot callback technology in two contact centers to reduce perceived wait time by at least 20%. A cross-functional task force will streamline phone authentication to a single-step verification process by June 2026. Digital content owners will revise top 25 billing FAQs and introduce contextual help within dispute workflows. Progress will be tracked bi-weekly, with target outcomes of raising voice NPS to +20 and reducing assisted-channel CES to 3.2 or lower by end of Q2.

structure.full_text:
Q1 2026 Customer Experience Performance Summary
Ref: CX-1401925-Q1 | Date: 07 April 2026 | From: Customer Insights & Journey Analytics

Section Executive Overview
For Q1 2026, overall Net Promoter Score (NPS) improved to +34, up 6 points quarter-over-quarter, primarily driven by higher satisfaction with digital self-service channels. Customer Satisfaction (CSAT) averaged 86%, while Customer Effort Score (CES, 1–5 scale) rose slightly to 3.4, indicating increased friction in assisted channels. Detractors are concentrated in contact-center interactions and late-stage service journeys. The results indicate strong digital momentum but persistent friction in human-assisted touchpoints.

Section Channel Performance Breakdown
Digital self-service (web and mobile app) achieved an NPS of +48 and CSAT of 91%, supported by faster login authentication and simplified account dashboards. In contrast, voice support NPS declined to +12, with CSAT at 78% and CES at 3.9, reflecting long hold times and repeat transfers. Live chat stabilized at +29 NPS with 84% CSAT, though sentiment flagged inconsistency in agent knowledge. Email support remained flat at +18 NPS with extended response times averaging 42 hours.

Section Verbatim Sentiment Themes
Promoters frequently cited ease of bill payment, intuitive navigation, and proactive outage notifications within the mobile app. Passives mentioned satisfactory issue resolution but inconsistent response speed when escalations were required. Detractors highlighted repeated authentication steps during phone calls, difficulty reaching a live agent, and confusion around service upgrade eligibility. Sentiment tagging shows a 22% increase in mentions of "long wait" and a 17% rise in comments referencing "being transferred multiple times."

Section Journey Pain Points
The onboarding journey shows friction during identity verification, where 14% of applicants abandon after document upload errors. In the billing dispute journey, 28% of customers contact support after failing to locate clarification in FAQs, signaling a content gap. Service outage resolution remains a key pain point, with customers reporting limited status transparency during restoration windows. These journey-stage breakdowns correlate strongly with detractor segments in post-interaction surveys.

Section 90-Day Improvement Action Plan
The CX team will pilot callback technology in two contact centers to reduce perceived wait time by at least 20%. A cross-functional task force will streamline phone authentication to a single-step verification process by June 2026. Digital content owners will revise top 25 billing FAQs and introduce contextual help within dispute workflows. Progress will be tracked bi-weekly, with target outcomes of raising voice NPS to +20 and reducing assisted-channel CES to 3.2 or lower by end of Q2.
